claims.statement: Open SWE is a LangGraph + Deep Agents coding-agent framework with an isolated sandbox per thread, plus separate reviewer and review-style analyzer graphs.
langgraph.json declares five graph entrypoints (agent, reviewer, analyzer, chat, scheduler) plus a FastAPI HTTP app (agent.webapp:app), all served together by langgraph dev.

Each langgraph.json graph key maps to a thin re-export module under agent/graphs/ that imports the underlying factory from its owning module (e.g. agent.graphs.agent:traced_agent re-exports agent.server:get_agent/traced_agent, and agent.graphs.scheduler:get_scheduler re-exports agent.scheduler:get_scheduler).

agent.webapp:app is a compatibility shim that re-exports the FastAPI app built in agent/api/app.py, which at startup mounts the dashboard router plus plan, workflow-approval, Linear, Slack, health, and GitHub webhook routers.

Open SWE accepts work from the dashboard, GitHub, Slack, Linear, and schedules; GitHub auto-review is considered for opened and ready_for_review pull requests only after the repository's auto-review and organization gates pass.

Python dependencies are managed with uv, and make targets provide the developer loop: install (uv sync --extra dev), dev (langgraph dev serving all graphs + FastAPI), run (uvicorn FastAPI-only), test (pytest), lint/format (ruff), and typecheck (ty).
Open SWE requires Python 3.14, langgraph.json serves Python 3.14, Ruff uses line-length 100, and pytest runs with asyncio_mode auto.
The JavaScript dashboard and desktop app use pnpm, with make web (pnpm run dev) running the ui/ dashboard and dev:desktop running the Electron wrapper.

Python implementations are async-first; a synchronous method is permitted only when an interface requires it, in which case it should raise NotImplementedError rather than introduce a parallel implementation.

The FastAPI lifespan pins a single event loop, validates sandbox and local-development LLM configuration before serving, and closes cached models at shutdown; credentialed CORS is installed only for configured dashboard origins and rejects a wildcard origin.

All Slack, Linear, GitHub, and dashboard triggers share dispatch_agent_run, which creates a durable LangGraph run for the selected agent or reviewer graph using a configurable thread id and defaults to an interrupt multitask strategy.

The reviewer is a non-mutating PR-review graph with finding tools, whereas the dashboard PR chat graph is sandbox-less and answers from seeded PR virtual files plus read-only GitHub-backed repository access.

The scheduler graph has one launch node that routes cron state to reconciliation, baby-sit watch evaluation, background-task monitoring, session-cost or agent-cost refresh, or a scheduled agent run, and reports missing required identifiers as result statuses.

A pre-existing unreachable main-agent sandbox is not automatically replaced because replacement could discard uncommitted work; a deleted sandbox is replaced, and only the reviewer opts into replacement of an unreachable sandbox because its checkout is recreated each run.

The shared pytest fixtures replace the agent store client with an in-memory implementation that preserves the production serialization path, clear the process-global TTL cache around each test, and default automatic review to enabled unless a test overrides the gate.

The Playwright end-to-end harness runs the real agent code, local sandbox, and local git remote while faking the LLM and external SaaS HTTP boundaries; root pnpm scripts provide browser and Electron end-to-end commands.
The root e2e setup command installs Chromium with Playwright dependencies, while browser tests run serially with one worker and the separate desktop configuration selects only the Electron spec.
dispatch_agent_run rejects a prebuilt run input when content, context, or source identity inputs are also provided, so callers must choose exactly one input-construction path.
